39	## Or adopt by hand
40	
41	To adopt an existing app by hand:
42	
43	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
44	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. 45	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
46	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
47	
48	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
49	
50	## Enable Partial Prefetching
51	
52	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
53	
54	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
55	
56	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
57	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
58	
59	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
60	  cacheComponents: true,
61	  partialPrefetching: true,
62	}
63	
64	export default nextConfig
65	```
66	
67	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
68	
69	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
70	
71	## What changes for `<Link>`
72	
73	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
74	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
75	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
76	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
78	
79	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
80	
81	## Migrate existing full prefetches
82	
83	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
84	
85	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
86	
87	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
88	
89	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
90	
91	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
92	
93	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
94	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
95	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
96	
97	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
98	  await page.goto('/products')
99	
100	  await instant(page, async () => {
101	    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
102	    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
103	    await link.click()
104	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
105	
106	    await expect(
107	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
108	    ).toBeVisible()
109	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
110	  })
111	})
112	```
113	
114	Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. 117	
118	The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:

120	```tsx filename="app/nav.tsx"

122	<Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
123	// After
124	<Link href="/about">About</Link>
125	```

267	### URL data
268	
269	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
270	
271	### Real-time content
272	
273	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
274	
275	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
276	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
277	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
278	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
279	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
280	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
281	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
282	
283	## Adopting incrementally
284	
285	Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
286	
287	Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. 578	title: Prefetching
579	description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
580	---
581	
582	Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.
583	
584	This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:
585	
586	- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
587	- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
588	- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
589	- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
590	
591	> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.
592	
593	## How does prefetching work?
594	
595	When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.
596	
597	Next.js automatically splits your application into smaller JavaScript chunks based on routes. Instead of loading all the code upfront like traditional SPAs, only the code needed for the current route is loaded. This reduces the initial load time while other parts of the app are loaded in the background. By the time you click the link, the resources for the new route have already been loaded into the browser cache.
598	
599	When navigating to the new page, there's no full page reload or browser loading spinner. Instead, Next.js performs a [client-side transition](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#client-side-transitions), making the page navigation feel instant.
600	
601	## What Next.js prefetches automatically
602	
603	Next.js prefetches automatically in production. As each `<Link>` enters the viewport, Next.js prefetches the route behind it and schedules the work so a page full of links doesn't flood the network. How much of each route it prefetches depends on whether the route is static or dynamic, and changes when [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) is enabled.
604	
605	### Prefetching static vs. dynamic routes
606	
607	Without Cache Components, a static route is prefetched in full, while a dynamic route is skipped unless it has a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) boundary.
608	
609	|                                                         | **Static page** | **Dynamic page**                                                                |
610	| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
611	| **Prefetched**                                          | Yes, full route | No, unless [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading)     |
612	| [**Client Cache TTL**](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) | 5 min (default) | Off, unless [enabled](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes) |
613	| **Server roundtrip on click**                           | No              | Yes, streamed after [shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching)                  |
614	
615	> **Good to know:** During the initial navigation, the browser fetches the HTML, JavaScript, and React Server Components (RSC) Payload. For subsequent navigations, the browser will fetch the RSC Payload for Server Components and JS bundle for Client Components.
616	
617	### Automatic prefetch
618	
619	```tsx filename="app/ui/nav-link.tsx" switcher
620	import Link from 'next/link'
621	
622	export default function NavLink() {
623	  return <Link href="/about">About</Link>
624	}
625	```
626	
627	```jsx filename="app/ui/nav-link.js" switcher
628	import Link from 'next/link'
629	
630	export default function NavLink() {
631	  return <Link href="/about">About</Link>
632	}
633	```
634	
635	| **Context**       | **Prefetched payload**           | **Client Cache TTL**                                                                              |
636	| ----------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
637	| No `loading.js`   | Entire page                      | 5 min ([`staleTimes.static`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes))           |
638	| With `loading.js` | Layout to first loading boundary | Off by default ([`staleTimes.dynamic`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) |
639	
640	Automatic prefetching runs only in production. Disable with `prefetch={false}` or use the wrapper in [Disabled Prefetch](#disabled-prefetch).
641	
642	### Prefetch scheduling
643	
644	Next.js maintains a small task queue, which prefetches in the following order:
645	
646	1. Links in the viewport
647	2. Links showing user intent (hover or touch)
648	3. Newer links replace older ones
649	4. Links scrolled off-screen are discarded
650	
651	The scheduler prioritizes likely navigations while minimizing unused downloads.
652	
653	> **Good to know**: With the **experimental** [`useOffline`](/docs/app/guides/offline-support) config enabled, pending prefetches resume through this queue when the app recovers from a connectivity drop.
654	
655	### Client cache
656	
657	Next.js stores prefetched React Server Component payloads in memory, keyed by route segments. When navigating between sibling routes (e.g. `/dashboard/settings` → `/dashboard/analytics`), Next.js reuses the parent layout and only fetches the updated leaf page.
658	
659	### Partial Prefetching
660	
661	With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) enabled via the [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) config (which requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching)), prefetching switches from the all-or-nothing model above to a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell):
662	
663	- **One shell per route, shared across links.** `<Link>` prefetches the route's App Shell, which holds its static and session output. Any number of links to the same route reuse that one shell, fetched once as the first link enters the viewport, so a page with many links makes fewer prefetch requests than prefetching each route in full.
664	- **The rest streams in.** Uncached data streams in after navigation, behind the shell's `<Suspense>` boundaries. A link can also resolve its URL data (`searchParams`, `params`) at prefetch time with [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
665	- **Invalidations refresh prefetches.** Data invalidations (`revalidateTag`, `revalidatePath`) silently refresh associated prefetches.
666	
667	See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the behavior change and the recommended adoption path. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) to resolve cached URL-specific content before navigation with `prefetch={true}`.
668	
669	## Controlling prefetching
670	
671	Next.js prefetches with defaults you can tune per link when they don't fit your resource budget or navigation patterns.
672	
673	### Manual prefetch
674	
675	To prefetch manually, import the `useRouter` hook from `next/navigation`, then call `router.prefetch()` to warm routes outside the viewport or in response to analytics, hover, or scroll.
676	
677	With [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching), `router.prefetch(href)` requests the same App Shell as a default `<Link>`. Pass `{ kind: 'full' }` to also request the per-link stage, matching `<Link prefetch={true}>`. The per-link stage can include cacheable content below [`await prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch).
678	
679	```tsx
680	'use client'
681	
682	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
683	import { CustomLink } from '@components/link'
684	
685	export function PricingCard() {
686	  const router = useRouter()
687	
688	  return (
689	    <div onMouseEnter={() => router.prefetch('/pricing', { kind: 'full' })}>
690	      {/* other UI elements */}
691	      <CustomLink href="/pricing">View Pricing</CustomLink>
692	    </div>
693	  )
694	}
695	```
696	
697	To prefetch a URL when a component loads, see [Extending or ejecting link](#extending-or-ejecting-link).
698	
699	### Hover-triggered prefetch
700	
701	> **Proceed with caution:** Extending `Link` opts you into maintaining prefetching, cache invalidation, and accessibility concerns. Do this only when the defaults are insufficient.
702	
703	By default, `<Link>` prefetches when it enters the viewport. To prefetch only the links a user is likely to visit, defer prefetching until they hover over a link:
704	
705	```tsx
706	'use client'
707	
708	import Link from 'next/link'
709	import { useState } from 'react'
710	
711	export function HoverPrefetchLink({
712	  href,
713	  children,
714	}: {
715	  href: string
716	  children: React.ReactNode
717	}) {
718	  const [active, setActive] = useState(false)
719	
720	  return (
721	    <Link
722	      href={href}
723	      prefetch={active ? null : false}
724	      onMouseEnter={() => setActive(true)}
725	    >
726	      {children}
727	    </Link>
728	  )
729	}
730	```
731	
732	`prefetch={null}` restores default prefetching once the user shows intent.
733	
734	With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), use `prefetch={active ? true : 'auto'}` instead. The `'auto'` value keeps the shared App Shell prefetched before the user shows intent, while `true` resolves cached URL-specific content before navigation after they do. Using `false` before intent disables the App Shell prefetch.
735	
736	### Extending or ejecting link
737	
738	You can extend the `<Link>` component to create your own custom prefetching strategy. For example, using the [ForesightJS](https://foresightjs.com/docs/integrations/nextjs) library which prefetches links by predicting the direction of the user's cursor.
739	
740	Alternatively, you can use [`useRouter`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router) to recreate some of the native `<Link>` behavior. However, be aware this opts you into maintaining prefetching and cache invalidation.
741	
742	```tsx
743	'use client'
744	
745	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
746	import { useEffect } from 'react'
747	
748	function ManualPrefetchLink({
749	  href,
750	  children,
751	}: {
752	  href: string
753	  children: React.ReactNode
754	}) {
755	  const router = useRouter()
756	
757	  useEffect(() => {
758	    let cancelled = false
759	    const poll = () => {
760	      if (!cancelled) router.prefetch(href, { onInvalidate: poll })
761	    }
762	    poll()
763	    return () => {
764	      cancelled = true
765	    }
766	  }, [href, router])
767	
768	  return (
769	    <a
770	      href={href}
771	      onClick={(event) => {
772	        event.preventDefault()
773	        router.push(href)
774	      }}
775	    >
776	      {children}
777	    </a>
778	  )
779	}
780	```
781	
782	Next.js invokes [`onInvalidate`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router#userouter) when it suspects cached data is stale, so you can refresh the prefetch.
783	
784	> **Good to know:** An `a` tag triggers a full page navigation. Use `onClick` to prevent it, then call `router.push` to navigate on the client.
785	
786	### Disabled prefetch
787	
788	You can fully disable prefetching for certain routes for more fine-grained control over resource consumption.
789	
790	```tsx
791	'use client'
792	
793	import Link, { LinkProps } from 'next/link'
794	
795	function NoPrefetchLink({
796	  prefetch,
797	  ...rest
798	}: LinkProps & { children: React.ReactNode }) {
799	  return <Link {...rest} prefetch={false} />
800	}
801	```
802	
803	For example, you may still want to have consistent usage of `<Link>` in your application, but links in your footer might not need to be prefetched when entering the viewport.

895	### Preventing too many prefetches
896	
897	Next.js automatically prefetches links in the viewport when using the `<Link>` component.

14	
15	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
16	
17	To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
18	
19	Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
20	
21	> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
22	
23	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
24	
25	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
26	
27	Install the skill:
28	
29	```bash filename="Terminal"
30	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
31	```
32	
33	Then give the agent this prompt:
34	
35	```prompt
36	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
37	```
38	
39	## Or adopt by hand
40	
41	To adopt an existing app by hand:
42	
43	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
44	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
45	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
46	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
47	
48	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
49	
50	## Enable Partial Prefetching
51	
52	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
53	
54	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
55	
56	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
57	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
58	
59	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
60	  cacheComponents: true,
61	  partialPrefetching: true,
62	}
63	
64	export default nextConfig
65	```
66	
67	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
68	
69	> **Good to know**: When `cacheComponents` is enabled without a `partialPrefetching` value, Next.js logs a warning asking you to set it to `true` or `false`. Set `false` only to keep the previous prefetch behavior while you work through this guide. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
70	
71	## What changes for `<Link>`
72	
73	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
74	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
75	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
76	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
78	
79	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
80	
81	## Migrate existing full prefetches
82	
83	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
84	
85	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
86	
87	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
88	
89	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
90	
91	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
92	
93	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
94	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
95	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
96	
97	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
98	  await page.goto('/products')
99	
100	  await instant(page, async () => {
101	    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
102	    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
103	    await link.click()
104	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
105	
106	    await expect(
107	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
108	    ).toBeVisible()
109	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
110	  })
111	})
112	```
113	
114	Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.

267	### URL data
268	
269	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
270	
271	### Real-time content
272	
273	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
274	
275	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
276	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
277	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
278	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
279	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
280	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
281	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

283	## Adopting incrementally
284	
285	Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.

287	Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. 362	## Move URL data behind Suspense

474	## Prefetching URL data
475	
476	Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) resolves it ahead of the click for links with `prefetch={true}`, at the cost of a server invocation per prefetchable link. To make the content resolvable at prefetch time, cache it behind the read with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). For a search page that reads `searchParams`:
477

481

483	  const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${query}`)
484	  return res.json()
485	}
486	
487	async function Results({
488	  searchParams,
489	}: Pick<PageProps<'/search'>, 'searchParams'>) {
490	  const { q } = await searchParams
491	  return <ResultList results={await getResults(q)} />
492	}
493	
494	export default function Page({ searchParams }: PageProps<'/search'>) {
495	  return (
496	    <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
497	      <Results searchParams={searchParams} />

578	title: Prefetching
579	description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
580	---
581	
582	Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.
583	
584	This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:
585	
586	- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
587	- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
588	- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
589	- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
590	
591	> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.
592	
593	## How does prefetching work?
594	
595	When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.
596	
597	Next.js automatically splits your application into smaller JavaScript chunks based on routes. Instead of loading all the code upfront like traditional SPAs, only the code needed for the current route is loaded. This reduces the initial load time while other parts of the app are loaded in the background. By the time you click the link, the resources for the new route have already been loaded into the browser cache.
598	
599	When navigating to the new page, there's no full page reload or browser loading spinner. Instead, Next.js performs a [client-side transition](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#client-side-transitions), making the page navigation feel instant.
600	
601	## What Next.js prefetches automatically
602	
603	Next.js prefetches automatically in production. As each `<Link>` enters the viewport, Next.js prefetches the route behind it and schedules the work so a page full of links doesn't flood the network. How much of each route it prefetches depends on whether the route is static or dynamic, and changes when [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) is enabled.
604	
605	### Prefetching static vs. dynamic routes
606	
607	Without Cache Components, a static route is prefetched in full, while a dynamic route is skipped unless it has a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) boundary.
608	
609	|                                                         | **Static page** | **Dynamic page**                                                                |
610	| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
611	| **Prefetched**                                          | Yes, full route | No, unless [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading)     |
612	| [**Client Cache TTL**](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) | 5 min (default) | Off, unless [enabled](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes) |
613	| **Server roundtrip on click**                           | No              | Yes, streamed after [shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching)                  |
614	
615	> **Good to know:** During the initial navigation, the browser fetches the HTML, JavaScript, and React Server Components (RSC) Payload. For subsequent navigations, the browser will fetch the RSC Payload for Server Components and JS bundle for Client Components.
616	
617	### Automatic prefetch
618	
619	```tsx filename="app/ui/nav-link.tsx" switcher
620	import Link from 'next/link'
621	
622	export default function NavLink() {
623	  return <Link href="/about">About</Link>
624	}
625	```
626	
627	```jsx filename="app/ui/nav-link.js" switcher
628	import Link from 'next/link'
629	
630	export default function NavLink() {
631	  return <Link href="/about">About</Link>
632	}
633	```
634	
635	| **Context**       | **Prefetched payload**           | **Client Cache TTL**                                                                              |
636	| ----------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
637	| No `loading.js`   | Entire page                      | 5 min ([`staleTimes.static`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes))           |
638	| With `loading.js` | Layout to first loading boundary | Off by default ([`staleTimes.dynamic`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) |
639	
640	Automatic prefetching runs only in production. Disable with `prefetch={false}` or use the wrapper in [Disabled Prefetch](#disabled-prefetch).
641	
642	### Prefetch scheduling
643	
644	Next.js maintains a small task queue, which prefetches in the following order:
645	
646	1. Links in the viewport
647	2. Links showing user intent (hover or touch)
648	3. Newer links replace older ones
649	4. Links scrolled off-screen are discarded
650	
651	The scheduler prioritizes likely navigations while minimizing unused downloads.
652	
653	> **Good to know**: With the **experimental** [`useOffline`](/docs/app/guides/offline-support) config enabled, pending prefetches resume through this queue when the app recovers from a connectivity drop.
654	
655	### Client cache
656	
657	Next.js stores prefetched React Server Component payloads in memory, keyed by route segments. When navigating between sibling routes (e.g. `/dashboard/settings` → `/dashboard/analytics`), Next.js reuses the parent layout and only fetches the updated leaf page.
658	
659	### Partial Prefetching
660	
661	With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) enabled via the [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) config (which requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching)), prefetching switches from the all-or-nothing model above to a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell):
662	
663	- **One shell per route, shared across links.** `<Link>` prefetches the route's App Shell, which holds its static and session output. Any number of links to the same route reuse that one shell, fetched once as the first link enters the viewport, so a page with many links makes fewer prefetch requests than prefetching each route in full.
664	- **The rest streams in.** Uncached data streams in after navigation, behind the shell's `<Suspense>` boundaries. A link can also resolve its URL data (`searchParams`, `params`) at prefetch time with [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
665	- **Invalidations refresh prefetches.** Data invalidations (`revalidateTag`, `revalidatePath`) silently refresh associated prefetches.
666	
667	See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the behavior change and the recommended adoption path. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) to resolve cached URL-specific content before navigation with `prefetch={true}`.
668	
669	## Controlling prefetching
670	
671	Next.js prefetches with defaults you can tune per link when they don't fit your resource budget or navigation patterns.
672	
673	### Manual prefetch
674	
675	To prefetch manually, import the `useRouter` hook from `next/navigation`, then call `router.prefetch()` to warm routes outside the viewport or in response to analytics, hover, or scroll.
676	
677	With [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching), `router.prefetch(href)` requests the same App Shell as a default `<Link>`. Pass `{ kind: 'full' }` to also request the per-link stage, matching `<Link prefetch={true}>`. The per-link stage can include cacheable content below [`await prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch).
678	
679	```tsx
680	'use client'
681	
682	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
683	import { CustomLink } from '@components/link'
684	
685	export function PricingCard() {
686	  const router = useRouter()
687	
688	  return (
689	    <div onMouseEnter={() => router.prefetch('/pricing', { kind: 'full' })}>
690	      {/* other UI elements */}
691	      <CustomLink href="/pricing">View Pricing</CustomLink>
692	    </div>
693	  )
694	}
695	```
696	
697	To prefetch a URL when a component loads, see [Extending or ejecting link](#extending-or-ejecting-link).
698	
699	### Hover-triggered prefetch
700	
701	> **Proceed with caution:** Extending `Link` opts you into maintaining prefetching, cache invalidation, and accessibility concerns. Do this only when the defaults are insufficient.
702	
703	By default, `<Link>` prefetches when it enters the viewport. To prefetch only the links a user is likely to visit, defer prefetching until they hover over a link:
704	
705	```tsx
706	'use client'
707	
708	import Link from 'next/link'
709	import { useState } from 'react'
710	
711	export function HoverPrefetchLink({
712	  href,
713	  children,
714	}: {
715	  href: string
716	  children: React.ReactNode
717	}) {
718	  const [active, setActive] = useState(false)
719	
720	  return (
721	    <Link
722	      href={href}
723	      prefetch={active ? null : false}
724	      onMouseEnter={() => setActive(true)}
725	    >
726	      {children}
727	    </Link>
728	  )
729	}
730	```
731	
732	`prefetch={null}` restores default prefetching once the user shows intent.
733	
734	With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), use `prefetch={active ? true : 'auto'}` instead. The `'auto'` value keeps the shared App Shell prefetched before the user shows intent, while `true` resolves cached URL-specific content before navigation after they do. Using `false` before intent disables the App Shell prefetch.
735	
736	### Extending or ejecting link
737	
738	You can extend the `<Link>` component to create your own custom prefetching strategy. For example, using the [ForesightJS](https://foresightjs.com/docs/integrations/nextjs) library which prefetches links by predicting the direction of the user's cursor.
739	
740	Alternatively, you can use [`useRouter`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router) to recreate some of the native `<Link>` behavior. However, be aware this opts you into maintaining prefetching and cache invalidation.
741	
742	```tsx
743	'use client'
744	
745	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
746	import { useEffect } from 'react'
747	
748	function ManualPrefetchLink({
749	  href,
750	  children,
751	}: {
752	  href: string
753	  children: React.ReactNode
754	}) {
755	  const router = useRouter()
756	
757	  useEffect(() => {
758	    let cancelled = false
759	    const poll = () => {
760	      if (!cancelled) router.prefetch(href, { onInvalidate: poll })
761	    }
762	    poll()
763	    return () => {
764	      cancelled = true
765	    }
766	  }, [href, router])
767	
768	  return (
769	    <a
770	      href={href}
771	      onClick={(event) => {
772	        event.preventDefault()
773	        router.push(href)
774	      }}
775	    >
776	      {children}
777	    </a>
778	  )
779	}
780	```
781	
782	Next.js invokes [`onInvalidate`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router#userouter) when it suspects cached data is stale, so you can refresh the prefetch.
783	
784	> **Good to know:** An `a` tag triggers a full page navigation. Use `onClick` to prevent it, then call `router.push` to navigate on the client.
785	
786	### Disabled prefetch
787	
788	You can fully disable prefetching for certain routes for more fine-grained control over resource consumption.
789	
790	```tsx
791	'use client'
792	
793	import Link, { LinkProps } from 'next/link'
794	
795	function NoPrefetchLink({
796	  prefetch,
797	  ...rest
798	}: LinkProps & { children: React.ReactNode }) {
799	  return <Link {...rest} prefetch={false} />
800	}
801	```
802	
803	For example, you may still want to have consistent usage of `<Link>` in your application, but links in your footer might not need to be prefetched when entering the viewport.
804	
805	## Troubleshooting
806	
807	### Triggering unwanted side-effects during prefetching
808	
809	If your layouts or pages are not [pure](https://react.dev/learn/keeping-components-pure#purity-components-as-formulas) and have side-effects (e.g. tracking analytics), Next.js might run them when the route is prefetched, not when the user visits the page.
810	
811	To avoid this, move side-effects to a `useEffect` hook or a Server Action triggered from a Client Component.
812	
813	**Before**:
814	
815	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher
816	import { trackPageView } from '@/lib/analytics'
817	
818	export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
819	  // This runs during prefetch
820	  trackPageView()
821	
822	  return <div>{children}</div>
823	}
824	```
825

828	
829	export default function Layout({ children }) {
830	  // This runs during prefetch
831	  trackPageView()
832	
833	  return <div>{children}</div>

835	```
836	
837	**After**:
838	
839	```tsx filename="app/ui/analytics-tracker.tsx" switcher

841	
842	import { useEffect } from 'react'
843	import { trackPageView } from '@/lib/analytics'
844	
845	export function AnalyticsTracker() {
846	  useEffect(() => {
847	    trackPageView()
848	  }, [])
849	
850	  return null
851	}
852	```

894	
895	### Preventing too many prefetches
896	
897	Next.js automatically prefetches links in the viewport when using the `<Link>` component.
898	
899	You might want to prevent this to avoid unnecessary resource usage, such as when rendering a large list of links (e.g. an infinite scroll table).

The project title now loads ahead of the click from the dashboard, and the description and activity list wait until the user actually navigates. I followed the "Optimizing prefetching" guide for the Next.js version in this repo.

**Changes:**

1. **`next.config.ts`**: turned on `partialPrefetching: true`. This makes the per-link prefetch stage available, which the other two changes need.

2. **`app/page.tsx`**: the dashboard links now use `prefetch={true}`. The title depends on `[slug]`, which differs for every link, so the shared route shell that a default link prefetches can't include it. `prefetch={true}` asks for a separate prefetch per link that can include cached data for that slug.

3. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`**: split into two parts, each with its own `<Suspense>`:
   - `<ProjectTitle>` reads `params` and calls the cached `getProjectTitle(slug)`, so the title is part of the per-link prefetch.
   - `<ProjectDetails>` starts with `await navigation()` from `next/cache`, which keeps it out of every prefetch. Its "Loading details..." placeholder is prefetched instead, and the slow (800ms) `getProjectDetails` call only runs once the user navigates. That data stays cached with `'use cache'`, so later visits reuse it.

When you click a project, the title appears immediately with "Loading details..." under it, and the description and activity list fill in afterwards.

**Checks:** `next build` succeeds, and `/projects/[slug]` builds as a partial prerender. I haven't run it in a browser; automatic prefetching only happens in production builds, not in `next dev`. The build also rewrote `tsconfig.json` on its own, and I reverted that so the diff only contains these changes.

**Trade-off:** `prefetch={true}` costs one server request per link visible on screen. That's fine with two projects, but on a long project list you'd want to prefetch on hover instead (the `prefetch={active ? true : 'auto'}` pattern in the prefetching guide).
